newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech end-Dec M2 up 7.8 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Czech end-Dec M2 up 7.8 percent yr/yr.

text.p: The Czech National Bank said on Thursday that its key measure of money supply, M2, was 7.8 percent higher year-on-year at the end of December, when large deposits connected to the 1995 equity expansion of SPT Telecom a.s. are factored into the equation.
It said that without factoring the SPT deposits, M2 was up 9.2 percent year-on-year.
The figures showed a slowing in M2 growth from November which showed a rise of 11.3 percent without the SPT factor, and 9.7 percent including the SPT deposits.
It said total volume of crown and foreign currency denominated loans at the end of December was up 10.6 percent, year-on-year, up from 10.5 percent in November.
Total end-December deposits, including the SPT factor, were up 7.1 percent, down from 8.8 percent year-on-year growth in November.
The CNB said the overall average interest rate at the end of December on all crown-denominated credit extended was 13.61 percent, down 25 basis points from November.
CZECH M2 MONEY DEC 1996 NOV 1996 DEC 1995
* Includes domestic deposits connected to the $1.32 billion equity expansion of SPT Telecom a.s. in the summer of 1995.
